claim: The WP1201 generation-1 whole-profile digest changes for any changed fact because every fact participates in one canonical payload. Requirement-scoped subset binding can reduce irrelevant invalidation without relaxing rejection of changes in required facts.

source_contract.observed_digest_rule: SHA256(canonical JSON of schema + collector_version + generation + complete sorted facts map)
source_contract.important_scope_note: The experiment independently reconstructed the observed digest contract; it did not import/execute the Frankenstein product module and therefore is not exact-source runtime evidence.

raw_dynamic_output_probe.method: Place a synthetic wpctl-status string containing a transient media-stream label into the exact pipewire_topology fact shape used by the observed source contract, then canonicalize the whole-profile payload.
raw_dynamic_output_probe.interpretation: The source contract stores successful command stdout as the fact value without field-specific parsing/redaction. This proves retention capability, not that every real wpctl output contains sensitive text.

reproduced_findings: Monolithic invalidation is structural, not hypothetical: every single-fact perturbation changes the whole-profile digest.
Requirement-scoped subsets can preserve unrelated bindings in the same perturbations while still changing on selected relevant fields.
The observed G1 field set has no stable HostScopeIdentity field and no BootScopeIdentity field.
Successful dynamic command output is retained as raw fact text under the current contract; volatile runtime output should therefore be separated or parsed before stable fingerprint use.
counterevidence: The experiment does not show that component binding is automatically safer overall. The proposed groups are research candidates, not accepted product policy, and a bad requirement map could incorrectly preserve stale evidence. The monolithic model is conservative and remains the safe baseline until a Trigger-4 ablation proves exact dependency maps.
next_gate: E4 F2 ablation candidate: implement no product-source change first, using fixtures/admission logic to compare monolithic versus exact requirement maps. Promotion requires zero false-preserve cases for requirement-relevant changes and measured reduction of irrelevant revalidation.
